description:
We are a multidisciplinary team of developers, data engineers, and 3D modelers united by a single conviction: data science and space exploration must not remain trapped in static documents or isolated 2D formats.

We are passionate about tackling frontier aerospace challenges where real physics meets high-performance software. With SOUTH MOON, we were not satisfied with simply creating an attractive visualization.
summary:
SouthMoon is a web-based mission engineering platform that transforms disparate NASA geospatial and astronomical datasets into a real-time, interactive 3D simulation environment. Its purpose is to predict the operational survivability of robotic and crewed landing modules under the extreme challenges of grazing illumination, orographic horizon occlusion, and thermal cold traps at the lunar South Pole.

We developed a deterministic analytical engine integrating high-resolution LOLA digital elevation models with JPL Horizons orbital ephemerides. The system computes 360° topocentric horizon masks, calculates solar flux incident vectors, and models direct-to-Earth (LoS) communication links over actual lunar terrain. It incorporates dynamic power subsystem budgets (photovoltaic yield and battery state-of-charge) coupled with automated contingency workflows (Rescue Lab) and the Michu pedagogical copilot.

The system's predictive accuracy is substantiated through historical backtesting protocols using primary flight data from missions like Chandrayaan-3 (ISRO/UN) and IM-1 Odysseus (NASA/LRO), validating computed visibility windows, telemetry bounds, and sunset profiles against empirical surface observations. SOUTH MOON bridges planetary science and operational engineering for the Artemis era.
details:
On the frontier where night has lasted for millennia, we built the compass to never lose the light.

SouthMoon is a data-driven mission engineering and simulation framework that evaluates the operational survivability of robotic and crewed lunar landers facing extreme topographic hazards. Built with React 18, Three.js (React Three Fiber), and Node.js, the platform implements a deterministic analytical engine that calculates 360° orographic horizon occlusions, direct-to-Earth communication line-of-sight (LoS), and dynamic photovoltaic-battery power balances to minimize mission-critical failure modes under physical constraints of power, link availability, and permanent shadows.

The model integrates high-resolution NASA LOLA elevation data (metric grid with spheroidal lunar curvature corrections), JPL Horizons orbital ephemerides (DE441/DE421 kernels), and contextual layers from LRO-WAC and Diviner to simulate real-world surface conditions. Each surface module simulates vertical solar array kinematics to maximize power yield under grazing polar sunlight, battery discharge dynamics to endure cryogenic nights, and direct communication constraints with the Deep Space Network (DSN).

The interactive 3D workbench enables users to inspect landing candidates, compare mission windows side-by-side, and test contingency replanning in real time through the Rescue Lab. The project's originality lies in coupling a rigorous, auditable scientific pipeline with Michu, an interpretive dual-architecture copilot (featuring offline deterministic heuristics and Gemini-powered generative assistance) that translates dense orbital telemetry into clear, actionable engineering insights. Furthermore, the simulation is substantiated by historical backtesting protocols validated against empirical flight telemetry from Chandrayaan-3 and IM-1 Odysseus.

Humanity’s return to the Lunar South Pole will only accelerate in the coming years; yet, a miscalculation in terrain shadow or an unforeseen communications blackout can doom a multi-million-dollar mission. SOUTH MOON democratizes high-precision aerospace mission design, equipping space agencies, commercial CLPS providers, and the academic community with a mission-critical tool for sustainable and permanent human exploration on the Moon.
